comparisons.peer_summary: The company defines purchase commitments as unconditional, legally binding obligations for goods or services, primarily inventory, excluding cancelable agreements or those with terms of one year or less.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose specific minimum purchase obligations. Intel's disclosure details a mandatory minimum purchase of factory output from Ireland SCIP with volume-related damages for non-compliance. Broadcom defines its own 'Purchase Commitments' as unconditional, legally binding obligations specifying fixed or minimum quantities to be purchased, primarily for inventory.

sentences.text: We will be required to purchase minimum quantities of the related factory output from Ireland SCIP, or we will be subject to pay certain volume-related damages to Ireland SCIP, beginning at the earlier of when construction is complete or Q3 2027.

Represent unconditional purchase obligations to purchase goods or services, primarily inventory, that are enforceable and legally binding on us and specify all significant terms, including fixed or minimum quantities to be purchased, price provisions, and the approximate timing of the transaction.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, the company had approximately $6.7 billion in noncancelable purchase obligations with remaining terms exceeding one year, primarily covering fixed or minimum quantity/price payments for goods, services, and property, plant, and equipment, with payments scheduled annually from 2025 through 2030 and thereafter.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose non-cancelable purchase obligations. Intel specifies obligations to purchase minimum quantities of factory output from Ireland SCIP. Micron discloses approximately $6.7 billion in noncancelable purchase obligations primarily covering fixed or minimum quantity and price payments for goods, services, and PP&E.

sentences.text: We will be required to purchase minimum quantities of the related factory output from Ireland SCIP, or we will be subject to pay certain volume-related damages to Ireland SCIP, beginning at the earlier of when construction is complete or Q3 2027.

As of August 29, 2024, we had noncancelable commitments with remaining contractual terms in excess of one year of approximately $6.7 billion for purchase obligations, of which approximately $1.7 billion will be due in 2025, $1.7 billion due in 2026, $1.0 billion due in 2027, $800 million due in 2028, $200 million due in 2029, and $1.3 billion due in 2030 and thereafter.
Purchase obligations primarily include payments for goods or services with either a fixed or minimum quantity and price, which includes payments for the acquisition of property, plant, and equipment.

comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation of Inventories and Provisions for Excess or Obsolete Inventory
comparisons.peer_summary: The audit identified the valuation of inventories, specifically provisions for excess or obsolete inventory and excess product purchase commitments, as a critical audit matter due to significant management judgment regarding future demand and market conditions assumptions, which in turn required significant auditor effort and subjective judgment.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA address 'excess product purchase commitments' as part of their financial disclosures. Intel outlines the obligation to purchase minimum quantities from Ireland SCIP. NVIDIA identifies provisions for excess product purchase commitments as a critical audit matter, noting significant outstanding inventory purchase and long-term supply obligations.

sentences.text: We will be required to purchase minimum quantities of the related factory output from Ireland SCIP, or we will be subject to pay certain volume-related damages to Ireland SCIP, beginning at the earlier of when construction is complete or Q3 2027.

As described in Notes 1, 10 and 13 to the consolidated financial statements, the Company charges cost of sales for inventory provisions to write-down inventory for excess or obsolete inventory and for excess product purchase commitments.

Most of the Company's inventory provisions relate to excess quantities of products, based on the Company's inventory levels and future product purchase commitments compared to assumptions about future demand and market conditions.

As of January 28, 2024, the Company's consolidated inventories balance was $5.3 billion and the Company's consolidated outstanding inventory purchase and long-term supply and capacity obligations balance was $16.1 billion, of which a significant portion relates to inventory purchase obligations.
